sidnfonds.body: Nyves was selected in March 2026 as a pioneer project by SIDNfonds, the Dutch organisation that supports innovative internet projects contributing to a stronger internet.
sidnfonds.grant: For this the project receives a grant of € 10,000. With this financial support the idea of Nyves can be developed into a proof-of-concept application.
sidnfonds.quote: "The project ‘Nyves’ aims to bring old Hyves profiles back to life with a modern, open web application based on the Nostr protocol. Users can easily reactivate, share and search their stored Hyves data. Nyves preserves digital heritage, strengthens data autonomy and shows how open protocols make the social web future-proof. It therefore aligns with goal 1 of the SIDN fund: A strong internet."

aos.donation: The And Other Stuff collective donated $15,000 to the project in October.
aos.quote: And Other Stuff (AOS) is a collective of people who build, imagine, organize, and experiment. Together, we create and steward freedom tech—open tools, protocols, and applications that strengthen human liberty. We enhance the Commons, explore the art of the possible, and empower people to build their own futures.
aos.divine: Divine is also part of the AOS collective. It is a platform that, among other things, brings old content from the Vine platform back to life.

protocols.platforms_subtitle: A technical approach to free speech
protocols.platforms_body: If you have read the article `protocols, not platforms` by Mike Masnick, you may have gained the insight that we can make social media less centralised. Several protocols offer us the option to create decentralised social networks. In such an ecosystem the interests disappear that today demand all our attention and break down our digital wellbeing.
protocols.nostr_subtitle: Notes and other Stuff Transmitted by Relays
protocols.nostr_body: An open protocol where anyone can distribute data via so-called events through a network of relays. No verification restrictions and no APIs. It is a grassroots project without a central intermediary pulling all the strings. All data can be requested and verified by anyone. Every event carries a digital signature, made with a cryptographic private key.

archive.heading: The public Hyves archive
archive.body: Right now we use the publicly available data of Hyves profiles collected by the Archive Team. This data is the source for all content that we convert into so-called nostr events. These events can then be retrieved from various relays. That is what the application on Nyves.nl currently does.

transcript.text: Let's bring Hyves back.
Profile by profile, note by note, picture by picture.
Before Hyves went dark, thousands of people backed up their profile with Hyves Backup.
That was a desktop app I built that stored all your Hyves content locally on your own computer.
Valuable content, valuable memories that form a digital memory and should be preserved.
My idea is to invite everyone who made a backup
to turn that backup back into a Hyves profile, through the app Nyves.
Just like Hyves Backup, this is a web app that runs locally in your browser,
with no server and no platform.
Because data is exchanged through what are called relays.
On Nyves you can also browse profiles and leave notes, just like before.
This is all made possible by a new social networking protocol called Nostr.
So yes, once again: Nyves is an app, and therefore not a platform.
With Nyves we can bring back the authentic feeling of social media.
Social media where connection comes first, where your friends and their content come first.
Social media without third parties, the platforms, doing all they can to grab as much attention as possible,
for commercial interests.
Nyves, with an N.
This is the idea I'd love to turn into a proof of concept.
Thank you.

Nyves restores and indexes profiles and related content from legacy platforms (such as Hyves) and publishes them as Nostr events so that they can be discovered again. The Web Application may index, display, surface, cache, transmit or host Nostr events and related media, and may display or link to externally hosted content. Unless expressly stated otherwise, Nyves does not own or control independent relays, third-party storage providers, archives or external hosts.

All third-party trademarks, logos and brand names that appear through the Web Application, including "Hyves", remain the property of their respective owners. blocks.h3: Who is responsible for your data

blocks.p: The controller responsible for the data processed through Nyves-controlled infrastructure is Sebastian Hagens, the publisher of Nyves, based in the Netherlands. He determines which data is processed, why and how. For questions about this Privacy Policy or about how your data is processed, you can contact us at info{'@'}sebastix.nl.

Nyves is a Web Application that runs locally in your browser. Data you publish to third-party relays is processed by the operators of those relays; they are responsible for that processing. Nyves is not the controller for that data, except for content on the Nyves-controlled relay (https://rely.nyves.nl).

Nyves is free, open-source software (AGPLv3 LICENSE) which runs as a web application. It is not a service. The profiles are not accounts. There are no Nyves accounts stored in a database. The developer has no access to data stored on your device while browsing the website.
Nyves lets you also browse content from third-party Nostr relays. Those relays host the content. They are independent of Nyves, with their own operators and their own policies.

Once broadcast, Nostr events may be stored or replicated across multiple independent relays, including relays Nyves does not own or control.

means any independently operated server implementing the Nostr protocol for receiving, storing, indexing, or redistributing Nostr events. Unless expressly stated otherwise, relays are not operated by Nyves.

means any Nostr event, media, metadata, username, profile information, or other material submitted, published, uploaded, linked, or otherwise made available by a user through the Web Application, whether hosted by Nyves or externally.

blocks.p: Anything you publish to a relay can be copied to other relays or clients. Once published, you should assume it cannot be reliably deleted from the network.

If you choose to sign in with Google, authentication is handled through the Nyves Pomegranate login flow. Nyves receives only the authentication token issued by Pomegranate's central server and your email address from Google. No other Google profile data is received. On first sign-in, a Nostr key pair is generated for you.

The web application Nyves does not host content, so the app cannot remove illegal content. Only relays hosting the content can remove it. If the content is on the Nyves relay (https://rely.nyves.nl), we can delete it.

Nyves may collect and process information in several categories. The categories of personal information collected may include identifiers (such as public keys or IP addresses), internet or network activity information, and user-generated content. We collect information you provide directly, including Nostr events, profile metadata, communications with Nyves, and reports submitted through the Web Application.

Configuration, cached events, keys, drafts, and other operational data live in the web application's local storage. Other applications cannot read it. You can wipe it by clearing the app's storage in your browser.

blocks.h3: How we use information and on what legal basis

blocks.p: We process the data described above only for the purposes set out below. Every processing operation relies on one of the legal bases in Article 6 of the GDPR.

dl.text: To load your profile, display and publish events and let the app run locally. Legal basis: performance of the agreement and your request (Art. 6(1)(b)).

To answer your questions about using Nyves. Send your question to info{'@'}nyves.nl. Legal basis: performance of the agreement (Art. 6(1)(b)) and our legitimate interest in providing good support (Art. 6(1)(f)).
To protect the Nyves-controlled infrastructure against spam, attacks and abuse. Legal basis: legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f)).
To understand how the Web Application is used and to improve it, via the self-hosted Matomo instance (matomo.sebastix.nl). Legal basis: legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f)); you can object to this.
To detect and fix errors and crashes in the Web Application, via the self-hosted GlitchTip instance (logs.sebastix.dev). Legal basis: legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f)).
To send you the emails you have signed up for, via the self-hosted ListMonk instance (mail.nyves.nl). Legal basis: your consent (Art. 6(1)(a)), which you can withdraw at any time.
If you choose it, to authenticate you and generate a Nostr keypair for you. Legal basis: your consent (Art. 6(1)(a)) and performance of your request (Art. 6(1)(b)).
To comply with legal obligations, such as removing illegal content on the Nyves-controlled relay. Legal basis: legal obligation (Art. 6(1)(c)).

blocks.p: Where we rely on a legitimate interest, you can object to that processing. Where we rely on your consent, you can withdraw it at any time by emailing info{'@'}sebastix.nl. Withdrawing consent does not affect the lawfulness of processing carried out before that moment.
Nyves retains information for as long as reasonably necessary to operate the Web Application, comply with legal obligations, enforce its Terms and and prevent abuse.

Retention periods may vary depending on the nature of the data, including logs, moderation records, reports, and backup data. Some information may be retained for longer periods where required for legal, safety, or dispute-resolution purposes.
Nyves has no obligation to retain user content and may remove or cease storing or displaying content at its discretion, subject to applicable law.

Content you publish is sent to relays as a Nostr event and can be stored there indefinitely, even if you delete the event in the Web Application or close your account. Each relay manages its own storage and deletion policy. You can set an expiration date per event (the expiration field from NIP-40); relays that support it can delete the event after that date. We cannot guarantee that any given relay will honour it.

For all other data stored within Nyves-controlled infrastructure, such as server and error-tracking logs, analytics and mailing list sign-ups, we keep it for as long as necessary for the purpose for which it was collected, and delete it afterwards. We keep your email address for a mailing list sign-up until you unsubscribe. We do not store data in your browser's local storage; it stays on your own device until you clear it yourself.

Under the GDPR you have a number of rights regarding your personal data. Because Nyves runs largely locally in your browser and keeps no accounts, you can also exercise some of them yourself, for example by clearing the app's local storage.

dl.text: You can request which personal data we process about you and receive a copy. Much of the data is visible directly in the Web Application itself, since it runs locally.
You can have incorrect or incomplete data corrected. You can edit and republish the profile metadata in your Nostr events yourself.

You can request deletion of your data. You can clear the app's local storage yourself through your browser. Content you have published to relays can be deleted with a deletion request (NIP-09); we cannot guarantee that a given relay will honour it.
You can ask us to temporarily restrict processing, for example while a request or an objection is being handled.
You can object to processing that we base on a legitimate interest, such as analytics and error reporting.
You can request your data in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format, or have it transferred.

Where processing is based on your consent (such as mailing list sign-ups or optional Google login), you can withdraw that consent at any time. This does not affect the lawfulness of processing carried out before that moment.
You can lodge a complaint with the Dutch Data Protection Authority (autoriteitpersoonsgegevens.nl) if you believe we process your data unlawfully.

blocks.p: You can submit a request or an objection by emailing info{'@'}sebastix.nl. We respond within one month. Because Nyves keeps no accounts, we cannot always link a request to a person; in that case we will let you know what we can do. Content that you or others have copied to third-party relays cannot be deleted by us; please contact that relay's operator instead.

blocks.h3: Cookies, local storage and data transfers

blocks.p: The Web Application uses your browser's local storage (localStorage) to keep your settings, keys, drafts and cached events. That data stays on your own device. In addition, the self-hosted Matomo instance (matomo.sebastix.nl) may set functional cookies to distinguish visits and to improve the Web Application. We do not set third-party advertising or tracking cookies.
You can refuse analytics by blocking cookies in your browser or using an ad blocker; the Web Application will keep working. You can clear the local storage at any time through your browser settings.

All services that Nyves uses, namely Matomo, GlitchTip and ListMonk, run on self-hosted servers in the Netherlands. No personal data is transferred to countries outside the EU/EEA. The only data that leaves our own infrastructure is the events you publish to relays yourself. The operators of those relays are responsible for that themselves; see also the definitions of Nostr and relay.
Nyves does not use automated decision-making or profiling that produces legal effects for you or otherwise significantly affects you.

Nyves implements reasonable technical and organizational measures to protect information processed on Nyves-controlled infrastructure. However, no system is completely secure, and Nyves does not guarantee that information will be free from unauthorized access, loss, or alteration.

If a data breach occurs involving personal data processed under our responsibility, we assess the risk and take appropriate measures to limit the consequences. If the breach is likely to pose a risk to your rights and freedoms, we report it to the Dutch Data Protection Authority and, where necessary, also inform you. Because Nyves keeps no accounts and most data stays in your browser, a breach can only affect Nyves-controlled infrastructure, such as server and error-tracking logs and mailing list sign-ups.

The Web Application does not address anyone under the age of 13. Nyves does not knowingly collect personal data from anyone under 13. If you are a parent or guardian aware that your child has provided the Nyves-controlled infrastructure with personal data, please contact us so it can be removed.

Because the Web Application interacts within a decentralized network connecting to relays, content may persist on independent relays, archives, or third-party systems even after it is removed from Nyves-controlled infrastructure. Nyves cannot guarantee deletion or control of such content.
We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. The current version is always on this page; the version number and the 'Last updated' date above are revised accordingly.

A new version takes effect 30 days after it is posted on this page, unless the law or an urgent security matter requires a shorter period. Until then the previous version continues to apply to data already collected.

Because Nyves keeps no accounts and does not collect visitors' email addresses, we cannot inform you directly about changes. For material changes we therefore post a clear notice on the homepage and on this page.

ontdek_profielen.seo_description: Discover some interesting profiles from the Nostrverse and Fediverse.
ontdek_profielen.title: Discover some interesting profiles
ontdek_profielen.intro: A list of profiles that are worth checking out.
ontdek_profielen.what_is_nostrverse_a1: The Nostrverse is the collection of relays, applications and people that together use the open Nostr protocol. Unlike a central platform, it has no owner: your identity is a key pair that is entirely yours, and your content is stored on relays of your choosing.
ontdek_profielen.what_is_nostrverse_a2: Because your profile, followers and posts are not tied to a single application, you can freely switch between different Nostr apps and still keep everything. Think of the difference between the telephone network and one specific app: the network stays, the app can be replaced.
ontdek_profielen.what_is_fediverse_a1: The Fediverse is the network of different platforms that can talk to each other through the open ActivityPub protocol, such as Mastodon, Pixelfed and PeerTube. Here too there is no central owner: anyone can start their own server, and those servers exchange messages with one another.
ontdek_profielen.what_is_fediverse_a2: The Fediverse and Nostr share the same ideals of decentralisation and user freedom, but use a different protocol. That is why we show profiles from both worlds side by side on this page.
ontdek_profielen.create_profile_q: How can I create a profile?
ontdek_profielen.create_profile_a1: Nyves itself cannot (yet) create a new profile or connect an existing one. In development: Nyves automatically gives you a guest profile that lets you reply and post. A guest profile is a real Nostr profile, but it only has a name and is removed after 7 days if you do not make it permanent.
ontdek_profielen.create_profile_a2: Would you like a lasting profile? Create one with a Nostr application such as {ditto}. Always keep your private key in a safe place: whoever holds that key has full access to your profile.
ontdek_profielen.create_design_q: How do I create a custom design for my profile?
ontdek_profielen.create_design_a1: Nyves supports so-called themes or custom designs for your profile. Such a design is stored in a Nostr event (kind 16767) that you create with an application that supports profile themes, such as {ditto}. In it you can set, among other things, the background colour or image, the text colours and the fonts used.
ontdek_profielen.create_design_a2: As soon as your profile has a custom design, a ‘Show custom design!’ button appears on your profile page, letting you switch back and forth between your own design and the Nyves default design. Looking for inspiration? Have a look at the profiles with a custom design.

a.hyves_fact_band: The Partysquad was the most played band: more than 8 million times in one year.
a.hyves_fact_friends: Gerard Joling was most popular with more than 290,000 friends.
a.hyves_fact_data: All the hosted data was around 2 petabytes. That was insane for a small country like the Netherlands.
a.hyves_fact_photos: On some days, more than 2 million photos were uploaded in a single day.
a.hyves_data: You can find answers in this article that VPNgids researched back in 2019:
a.mediahuis_data: According to {link}, Mediahuis may still have all the login credentials. In 2018 Hyves Games was sold to Azerion, and all the data moved with it, except the passwords.
a.difference: You can find the answer to this question on {link}.
a.nostrverse_1: The Nostrverse is the whole of relays, applications and people that together use the open Nostr protocol. Unlike a central platform, there is no owner: your identity is a keypair that is entirely yours, and your content is stored on relays that you choose.
a.nostrverse_2: Because your profile, followers and messages are not tied to a single application, you can switch freely between different Nostr apps and still keep everything. Think of the difference between the telephone network and one specific app: the network stays, the app can be replaced.
a.fediverse_1: The Fediverse is the network of different platforms that can talk to each other via the open ActivityPub protocol, such as Mastodon, Pixelfed and PeerTube. Here too there is no central owner: anyone can start their own server and those servers exchange messages with each other.
a.fediverse_2: The Fediverse and Nostr share the same ideals of decentralisation and user freedom, but use a different protocol. That is why we show profiles from both worlds side by side on the page {link}.
a.keypairs: At the moment these keypairs are managed by Sebastian Hagens, who develops the Nyves application.

over_nyves.hvsbackup_body: Between 2010 and 2013 Sebastian Hagens developed an application called HVSbackup{link} that let you download various parts of your Hyves profile.

over_nyves.archive_body: A few months before Hyves went offline as a social network, thousands of people made a backup of their Hyves profile with the application. Besides these backups, a large backup was also made as a public archive by the Archive Team of The Internet Archive{link}. These sources can be used to bring Hyves back. Not as a central platform, however, but purely as an application that fetches all content from so-called relays.

over_nyves.why_body: We want to preserve Hyves as a piece of cultural digital heritage. On top of that, Nyves is an application that uses an open network where you as an individual have full autonomy over your data.
over_nyves.nostr_title: Let's fix the web - nostr by default
over_nyves.nostr_body1: Since Sebastian has been online on the internet (1998), he is highly interested in online communities, social networking and new ways of digital interactions. The internet has changed radically in the last decade and that change is not serving our interests. It's fair to say the web is broken in many ways. With Nostr we can fix this.

difference.seo_title: What is the difference between Nyves and Hyves | Blog
difference.seo_description: The N in Nyves stands for nostr. Nyves is not a platform.
difference.title: What is the difference between Nyves and Hyves?
difference.intro_short: The short answer is simple: 1 letter ;-) The N in Nyves stands for nostr.
difference.intro_long: The long answer is a bit more complicated.
difference.nostr_body: Nostr is an abbreviation that stands for Notes and Other Stuff Transmitted by Relays. It is an open protocol, much like e-mail. It is a simple protocol that describes how you send messages between applications and relays. There is an open network on which anyone can build applications. Nyves is one such application.
difference.archive_body: With Nyves you can look up and view old Hyves profiles. They were archived by {link} before Hyves went dark as a social network. This archive was rebuilt especially for Nyves, based on the available data that you can also find via The Wayback Machine.
difference.heritage_body: Hyves gave rise to many memories, and that is why these traces of the past are worth preserving. Let's not forget how social Hyves was, before social media became antisocial in the period after Hyves. We safeguard this piece of collective memory by making all of Hyves' content available through nostr relays.
difference.interoperable_body_1: Because an open protocol is used, there are agreements about how all messages exchanged between relays and applications are formatted. In principle anyone can communicate with a relay. Your profile is not tied specifically to the Nyves application, but will also work in other nostr applications.
difference.interoperable_body_2: All data is interoperable; that gives you the freedom to choose other applications that best suit your wishes and needs.
difference.no_accounts_body: Nyves does not work with accounts, but with profiles based on so-called keypairs. So you have no username and password stored somewhere in a central, closed-off place. What you do have is a public and a secret key with which you can identify yourself, or with which others can verify you. A keypair has been created for every Hyves profile. Every piece of content belonging to a profile carries a digital signature. Anyone can see and verify it, so you can be sure that the content really belongs to that profile.
difference.no_database_body: Because all data is sent via relays, there is no central place where all data is stored. These relays are simple servers and are located anywhere in the world where there is an internet connection. At the moment there are several thousand relays that do nothing but send messages between applications.
difference.opensource_body: All code of the Nyves application and relay can be inspected by anyone thanks to the AGPLv2 licence. Everyone is free to make a copy of this code, for example to build a variant of the Nyves application or to set up their own relay to send their messages to.
difference.build_in_public_body: Nyves is developed in public. Anyone can see what is being developed. The backlog with epics and user stories is public, so you can see what is being worked on.
difference.autonomy_body: Thanks to the open network there is no central intermediary connecting all people, like Facebook, TikTok, WhatsApp, Instagram or Hyves. With Nyves we are redefining social media. It is a decentralised network where power lies with the individual. In such a network, the interests that demand all our attention today and break down our digital well-being disappear.
difference.dutch_project_body: Nyves is an idea being developed by a Dutchman, in the Netherlands itself. Both the application on nyves.nl and the relay on rely.nyves.nl run on a server in the Netherlands.
